facts.text: My vision has been getting worse.
It has been slowly declining ever since my cataract surgery two years ago.
It has got worse over the past several months, most noticeably over the last three months.
Light bothers both of my eyes.
I had cataract surgery two years ago.
I've had open-angle glaucoma for 25 years.
For the last seven years my glaucoma has been treated with brimonidine 0.1% drops, twice a day in both eyes.
I haven't had any problems with my eyelids.
I've never had any disease of the cornea.
Apart from my eyes, I don't have any medical problems.
Apart from my eyes, I don't have any other symptoms.

findings.name: visual acuity
findings.result: Best-corrected distance visual acuity 20/60 in the right eye and 20/70 in the left eye.

findings.name: slit-lamp examination
findings.result: Dermatochalasis; superficial punctate keratitis; bilateral peripheral corneal opacities from the 4- to 5-o'clock and 7- to 8-o'clock positions with overlying neovascularization; crocodile shagreen bilaterally; no guttata or lattice lines.

findings.name: dilated fundus examination
findings.result: Blunted macular reflex in both eyes; cup-to-disc ratio 0.65 in the right eye and 0.75 in the left eye.

findings.name: autoimmune serology
findings.result: ANA negative; c-ANCA negative; p-ANCA negative; rheumatoid factor negative; anti-SSA/Ro negative; anti-SSB/La negative.

gold.reasoning: 1. Infectious keratitis — “All tests resulted as negative or within normal limits.” 2. Autoimmune-associated keratitis (e.g., RA, SLE, Sjögren) — “The patient's PCP reported no findings in the review of systems or on physical exam consistent with rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjogren syndrome, or other similar systemic diseases.” 3. Corneal arcus — “Corneal arcus, unlike LK, does not typically affect visual acuity as the central cornea is spared.” 4. Schnyder corneal dystrophy — “Bilateral corneal opacification may also be seen with Schnyder corneal dystrophy (SCD), a rare inherited disorder of the stroma.” 5. Corneal xanthoma and systemic lipid disorders (e.g., Tangier disease, familial HDL disorders) — “Although these are less common and lack neovascularization.” 6. Drug-induced lipid keratopathy from brimonidine use — “We have concluded that the BT is the most likely cause of this patient's lipid keratopathy.”

source_issues: The patient denied lid disorders (s003), but slit-lamp examination found dermatochalasis (s008).
The refraction uses en dashes for minus cylinders.
s011 lists the primary care physician's review for systemic rheumatologic disease alongside the tests; it is not an orderable test.
notes: Index visit: the referral visit for several months of worsening vision (s001); the infectious and autoimmune workup (s011–s012) belongs to the same evaluation.

The primary care physician's review for systemic rheumatologic disease (s011) is not given its own finding; its negative result is reflected in f014 (no systemic symptoms) and f013 (no systemic disease).
f013 is 'other medical problems' rather than 'chronic medical problems' because she has glaucoma and past cataract surgery.
Corneal opacities, keratitis and fundus findings need a slit lamp or fundoscopy, so they are findings only; the patient-noticeable sign is the worsening vision (f001) and light sensitivity (f004).
Fixes: f007 alias 'eye drops' removed; f008 alias 'eye drops' removed.
